headline: AI will make and break companies — exponential upside and downside risk means every business must list AI on its compliance risk register
reasoning: Sam Riley argues that AI is a transformative but double-edged technology: it can deliver expert-level speed and capability but, when misused or mismanaged, scales damage exponentially. He cites the Auditor General's finding that Services Australia — the agency from which Medicare data was accessed — did not have a dedicated AI risk line on its compliance risk register, calling this a basic governance failure every organisation must now address. His core advice is to prioritise AI risk by likelihood of business impact rather than spreading resources indiscriminately, because competitors who use AI effectively will erode the margins of those who do not.
quote: It's exactly like any new tech. You know, we made fire whenever we did that years ago. It can cook your food, keep you warm, or it can burn your village down. And it's the same thing with AI. It can do marvellous things. It's an expert. It's so fast, but used in the wrong way. It scales exponentially and causes exponential damage.
episode_title: The AI risks businesses are missing
